Credit Card Calculator

A credit card payoff calculator calculates the exact number of months and total interest required to eliminate your revolving balance. It directly compares paying only the lender minimum requirement against fixed monthly payments, illustrating how small extra amounts can cut years of repayment and thousands in financing costs.
Interactive Credit Card CalculatorInstant In-Browser Calculation

Formula and Calculation Method

Credit card interest accrues daily based on the average daily balance:

Monthly Interest = Balance × (APR ÷ 365) × Days in Month
New Balance = Balance + Monthly Interest - Payment

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Payoff Comparison ($8,000 Balance at 22% APR)
Input Values:
  • Current Balance: $8,000
  • Annual Percentage Rate (APR): 22.0%
  • Option A (Minimum): Greater of $25 or 2% of balance + interest ($220 initial)
  • Option B (Fixed Payment): $300 / month

1. Option A (Minimums only): Takes 242 months (over 20 years) to extinguish, costing $9,480.12 in interest. Total repaid: $17,480.12.

2. Option B (Fixed $300/mo): Fully eliminated in 37 months (3.1 years), costing $3,042.85 in interest. Total repaid: $11,042.85.

3. Savings: Accelerating payment saves $6,437.27 in interest and frees you 17 years sooner.

Result: Fixed $300/mo pays off in 37 months, saving $6,437.27 in interest.

How to Use the Credit Card Calculator

  1. Enter your total current credit card balance.
  2. Enter the card APR interest rate from your latest billing statement.
  3. Provide your minimum payment percentage or fixed target monthly payment.
  4. Review the debt-free payoff date, total interest charges, and monthly reduction chart.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • Assumes you make no new purchases or balance transfers on the card during the payoff period.
  • Does not account for variable APR rate hikes initiated by the credit card issuer or late payment penalties.

Frequently Asked Questions About Credit Card Calculator

How long does it take to pay off a credit card paying only the minimum?

Because minimum payments decline alongside the balance, paying only the minimum on a $5,000 balance at 22% APR typically requires 15 to 19 years and more than $6,000 in interest alone.

Why does paying only the minimum take so long?

Minimum payments are typically set at just 1% to 2% of the principal balance plus accrued monthly interest. As the principal drops, the required minimum drops as well, causing the vast majority of each payment to service interest rather than eliminate debt.

How is daily credit card interest calculated?

Card issuers divide your APR by 365 to determine your daily periodic rate. This rate is multiplied by your average daily balance and the number of days in the billing cycle to calculate monthly finance charges.

What is the best strategy to pay off multiple credit cards?

The two primary methods are the Debt Avalanche (paying highest APR first to minimize total interest) and the Debt Snowball (paying smallest balances first for psychological momentum). Use our Debt Payoff Calculator to compare both.

Will paying off my credit card hurt my credit score?

No. Paying down revolving credit balances lowers your credit utilization ratio, which is one of the highest weighted factors (30%) in FICO and VantageScore scoring models, generally improving your score.

How much interest can I save by paying an extra $50 a month?

On an $8,000 balance at 22% APR, adding just $50 to a $250 monthly payment saves over $1,100 in interest and eliminates the debt 8 months earlier.
